summary: The Police Media Division said the Ministry's official website had been targeted by external parties.
confirmed_details: Police Media Division statement, as reported by Ada Derana: there were multiple instances of unauthorized access; irregularities were then noticed in how the state emblem was displayed on the site.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: The dates of the access were not given. Whether any data was accessed is not stated. The method is not stated.
investigation_announced: On the Minister's instruction the Ministry Secretary filed a complaint with the CID on 9 January 2026; the CID opened a formal investigation; the Ministry began an internal inquiry.
remediation_confirmed: Sri Lanka CERT and ICTA took measures to restore the website, according to the police statement. Daily FT adds that its security was reinforced.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: Does not indicate the site's present state.

summary: The Department's website was hacked and its content altered.
confirmed_details: Sri Lanka CERT confirmed the hack and that content was altered. A named CERT engineer told the Sunday Times (5 January 2025) that CERT's audit found critical vulnerabilities in the old website and that CERT recommended replacing it. The Government Printer said certain weaknesses had been identified and that a new site would be audited by CERT before going live.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: Reports differ on the date (night of 30 December or 31 December 2024). The nature of the weaknesses was not published and is not recorded here.
investigation_announced: The Cabinet spokesman announced investigations on 31 December 2024. The police spokesman said on 2 February 2025 that investigations were continuing with no arrests.
remediation_confirmed: CERT said the site was restored on 2 January 2025. Core documents were back online by 2 February 2025 without the old features. A replacement site was to be procured; whether it has gone live was not found.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: The reported audit findings concern the old website. They say nothing about the current one.

summary: The Ministry's website homepage was defaced.
confirmed_details: The Sri Lanka Air Force Cyber Security Centre said the websites of the Ministry and of the Foreign Employment Bureau were attacked and their homepages defaced.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: Attribution was not established in the report read.
remediation_confirmed: None found.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: More than six years old. The ministry's name and site have changed since.

summary: A cyberattack on the Ministry's website was acknowledged after data said to come from it was offered for sale online.
confirmed_details: Minister's statements, as reported by Ada Derana: a complaint about an apparent cyberattack on the official website was lodged with the CID through the Ministry Secretary; no highly sensitive information was compromised; only general public information appears to have been accessed by third parties.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: A listing dated 17 April 2026 on an underground forum claimed to offer data from the site, and press reports describe it as containing officers' names, email addresses and contact numbers. This has not been officially confirmed. That Sri Lanka CERT opened a separate inquiry is stated by the article without attribution.
investigation_announced: CID complaint lodged and CID tasked with investigating, per the Minister (reported 24 April 2026).
remediation_confirmed: None found.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: The incident is confirmed by the Minister; the description of the data is alleged.

summary: Files attached to regulatory applications were deleted from the Authority's document system hosted on the Lanka Government Cloud.
confirmed_details: The loss was discovered on 9 July 2021. Police said on 28 September 2021 that the CID arrested an engineer of the contracted IT vendor.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: Police said the deletion was intentional; the vendor had earlier described it as an error; a state counsel suggested a wider conspiracy in court. None of these was established in any source read. Press reports said no backup of the files existed.
investigation_announced: CID investigation with university forensic assistance (2021); arrest and remand reported.
remediation_confirmed: None confirmed. Recovery efforts were reported from October 2021; their result was not found.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: An insider or contractor data-deletion and backup failure in a back-end system. It was not an attack on the public website.

summary: The Department warned of fake websites imitating its online visa site.
confirmed_details: The Department said it had received reports of people paying fake websites and advised applicants to reach the visa site through the link on immigration.gov.lk.
remediation_confirmed: Public advisory issued by the Department.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: Fraud by third parties. Not a compromise of any government system.

summary: A traveller publicly alleged exposure of personal data connected with the visa issuance system then in use.
confirmed_details: The Secretary to the Ministry of Public Security said the Ministry was concerned and had asked the Department to look into it, as reported by Daily Mirror.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: The existence, cause and scope of any exposure were not confirmed in the report read. The article's exact date was not captured.
investigation_announced: The Ministry Secretary said the Department had been asked to look into the matter.
remediation_confirmed: None found.
label: POTENTIAL RISK - NOT VERIFIED
notes: Concerns an outsourced visa system, not immigration.gov.lk. Out of scope.

summary: An IT engineer told the Sunday Times that the ETA visa status page lacked sufficient verification before showing application details.
confirmed_details: The claim was published by the Sunday Times.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: The claim has not been confirmed by the Department or Sri Lanka CERT in any source read. No detail is recorded here and none was tested.
remediation_confirmed: None found.
label: POTENTIAL RISK - NOT VERIFIED
notes: Concerns the ETA application, which is out of scope. NOT TESTED and not to be tested without written authorization.

summary: The Department announced a system problem that stopped ETA approval notices being issued.
confirmed_details: The Department published a notice to applicants on 18 February 2026.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: No cause was stated. Nothing links the outage to a cyber incident.
remediation_confirmed: Temporary processing measures announced by the Department.
label: NO PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE
notes: Recorded only to show that no cyber cause is evidenced. Out-of-scope system.

summary: A disruption of the Lanka Government Cloud interrupted online services of more than 30 government institutions for over a week.
confirmed_details: ICTA announced the disruption on 13 October 2025 and its full resolution on 21 October 2025, and said data security and integrity were not compromised. The Department of Motor Traffic said its own operations were not interrupted; a provincial revenue-licence system was among those affected.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: ICTA described a technical and capacity problem. Press speculation about a possible breach was not supported by any official statement read.
investigation_announced: None announced as a cyber investigation.
remediation_confirmed: ICTA announced full restoration on 21 October 2025.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: An availability incident. No public evidence of a cyber cause.

summary: Railway authorities said the official website was hit by a cyberattack that affected its train timetable section.
confirmed_details: Railway officials said the attack affected only the online timetable section, which was disabled as a precaution. The Minister of Transport said on social media that the newly launched site was targeted by thousands of attacks within hours of launch and stayed operational.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: The type of attack is not stated. The site's launch date is not given. News 1st reported the website back online on 15 June, while Daily FT reported on 17 June that work to restore the timetable section was continuing.
investigation_announced: None found. No report read mentions an inquiry or Sri Lanka CERT.
remediation_confirmed: The affected section was disabled; the Department said the website was back online on 15 June 2026. Restoration of the timetable section was not confirmed in the sources read.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: Does not indicate the site's present state.

summary: Sri Lanka Railways warned of fraudulent websites posing as its ticket-booking platform.
confirmed_details: Sri Lankan diplomatic missions published the Department's notice advising visitors to use only the official reservation site.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: The notice's original date was not captured.
remediation_confirmed: Public advisory issued.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: Fraud by third parties. Not a compromise of any government system.

summary: A ransomware attack on the government cloud caused loss of email data for offices using gov.lk email addresses.
confirmed_details: ICTA confirmed that about 5,000 gov.lk email addresses were affected and that data from 17 May to 26 August 2023 was lost because no backup existed for that period. The CID opened an investigation.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: Which of the ten institutions lost data is not stated in any source read.
remediation_confirmed: None confirmed. Recovery efforts by ICTA and Sri Lanka CERT were reported.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: Affected email, not websites. Not attributed here to any single institution.

summary: Sri Lanka CERT was reported to warn of telephone callers impersonating Department officials.
confirmed_details: Hiru News reported the warning and that the Department does not send payment links to taxpayers.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: CERT's own notice was not located.
remediation_confirmed: Public advisory issued.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: Fraud by third parties. See IRD-PUB-17 in the IRD public evidence review.

institution: Sri Lanka Police (agency under the Ministry)
summary: Official social media accounts of the Sri Lanka Police, including its YouTube channel, were taken over.
confirmed_details: The Police spokesman confirmed the takeover and later said the Police website itself was not compromised.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: Attribution to foreign actors was stated by police as a suspicion.
investigation_announced: Police and Sri Lanka CERT inquiries reported.
remediation_confirmed: Police said the accounts were recovered, the YouTube channel last.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
notes: Concerns a separate agency and third-party platforms, not pubsec.gov.lk.

summary: No report of a compromise of the Department's website or tax system was found.
remediation_confirmed: Not applicable.
label: NO PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE
notes: A search miss is not proof that no incident occurred.

summary: No report of a cyber incident affecting the Department's website was found. Reported system failures were attributed to technical causes.
remediation_confirmed: Not applicable.

remediation_confirmed: Not applicable.

summary: The Ministry's official website was accessed without authorization and a message was posted on it.
confirmed_details: The Ministry acknowledged the incident in a statement reported on 5 April 2024 and apologized to users. Attributed to Sri Lanka CERT: Senior Information Security Engineer Charuka Damunupola, as reported by Daily Mirror on 10 April 2024, said CERT's initial investigation indicated a local individual was responsible and that a report would go to the Minister; Daily News (12 April 2024) reported him as saying the attack came from an internet connection within Sri Lanka. Daily Mirror (10 April 2024) also reports that SLCERT recommended launching a new website with updated security instead of reinstating the compromised one.
alleged_or_unconfirmed_details: Unattributed: the 10 April 2024 Daily Mirror article states, in the passive and without naming a source, that security patches and updates had not been applied and that the Ministry had not carried out the annual vulnerability assessment SLCERT had advised. These are recorded as the newspaper's reporting, not as a CERT statement. The posted message claimed to come from a student and asserted security flaws; the author's identity was not established. A Ministry official told Ceylon Today that no Ministry information was compromised. Date discrepancy: the Ministry and Newswire give 4 April 2024; Daily News reports the CERT engineer as giving 5 April. Sri Lanka CERT's own statement or report was not found.
investigation_announced: The Ministry's statement, reported on 5 April 2024, said Sri Lanka CERT and the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission were among those conducting a probe. On 10 April 2024 CERT was reported as saying its report would go to the Minister; Daily News (12 April 2024) reported that steps were being taken to submit it to the CID.
remediation_confirmed: A Ministry official said the site was restored on 5 April 2024. On 10 April 2024 the site was reported as due to return with basic features. Whether a new website was later launched, as CERT recommended, was not found.
label: CONFIRMED HISTORICAL INCIDENT
sources_opened: PRIMARY SOURCE URL OPENED 2026-11-11; RE-CHECKED AGAINST SEARCH EXCERPTS 2026-11-12
notes: The incident date (4 April 2024) comes from the Ministry statement and same-day reporting; the publication date is that of the main source, Daily Mirror, 10 April 2024. The reported statements describe the website as it was before April 2024. Current website security status: UNKNOWN.
